mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney authorizing the Luxembourg representative or proposed SCSp manager to execute the partnership agreement (acte de société / LPA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent legal authority in the signatory's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or proof of source of funds for any capital contribution and for the registered-office retainer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated financial institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the EU Council Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists where US nexus exists, and Luxembourg national asset-freeze measures. PEP categorization and enhanced due diligence must follow the amended Law of 12 November 2004, FATF Recommendations, and CSSF guidance. For a low-risk PR communications agency, simplified due diligence may apply after documentary risk assessment, but identification of the shareholder chain and UBOs is never waived. All screening and decision records must be retained in the AML/CFT client file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in Latin script using any language, but French is the administrative working language for RCS filings. The proposed name must be unique within the RCS, not misleading, not contrary to public order, and must not infringe existing trademarks. A non-Latin script name must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a certified translation; only the Latin-script statutory name is registered. A Société en Commandite Spéciale must clearly bear the legal form indicator 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BOURSE / STOCK EXCHANGE / CLEARING HOUSE / CHAMBRE DE COMPENSATION
SICAV / SICAF / OPCVM / INVESTMENT FUND / FONDS D'INVESTISSEMENT
SOCIÉTÉ ANONYME / SA / SARL / EUROPEAN COMPANY / SE / SCA when not the actual corporate form
Words falsely suggesting Luxembourg sovereign affiliation, public institution, or regulated professional activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal or request to the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of the refusal notice, providing legal arguments that the proposed name is not confusing and does not violate the Commercial Companies Law. For names containing sensitive ministerial tokens, an express prior authorization from the competent minister must first be obtained. In parallel, the applicant may file a fresh reservation with a structurally different name that avoids the prohibited token. Appeal to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) remains available where the administrative refusal is legally contestable. Practically, the fastest remedy is to file an alternative name reservation before the fee is disbursed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A serviced office or co-working address in Luxembourg may be used as the registered office if it is a physical place at the disposal of the company, is located in the Grand Duchy, and is not a mere letterbox inconsistent with actual economic substance. A pure virtual office without on-site management or mail handling is not advisable for an international PR agency, as it could trigger substance challenge by the Luxembourg tax administration and increase AML inspection risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a standard low-risk PR communications firm; approximately 10-15% chance of an unannounced or announced on-site inspection during the first year. The probability increases materially if there are UBO disclosure inconsistencies, nominee relationships, high-risk country ties, PEP exposure, unreliable registered-office answers, or unexplained cash or wire flows.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Article 106 (société en commandite spéciale); Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to trades (autorisation d'établissement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 5, rue Plaetis, L-2338 Luxembourg; online filing at lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive deed of the special limited partnership (acte constitutif / statuts de la société en commandite spéciale) submitted through the RCS electronic filing form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no statutory escrow account requirement for an SCSp; contributions may be in cash, kind or services as set out in the partnership deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the special limited partnership SCSp is constituted under the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915, as amended, by the general partner and the limited partners having subscribed to the partnership units as set out in the register of partners; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp is established at [registered address], Luxembourg, and may be relocated by the general partner upon such formalities as may be required by law; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed general partner and manager, with sole power to represent the SCSp in all dealings, to open bank accounts, and to execute agreements; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the statutory filing, RESA publication, and registration before the Luxembourg Business Registers are hereby approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the constitutive deed of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary (if notarization is elected) or the partners themselves; no governmental pre-clearance is required at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign, by private deed or by notarial deed, the partnership agreement identifying the general partner, the initial limited partner(s), the partnership name, the registered office in Luxembourg, the object of the enterprise, the subscription commitments, and the management provisions. Keep the signed deed and the partners' register ready for electronic transmission to the Luxembourg Business Registers.
required_dossiers: Register of partners and capital contributions
Identity documents of all partners and managers
Registered office consent letter or lease of premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is defective, the partners may supplement or amend it by a rectification deed signed by the same parties before the RCS filing is validated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the constitutive documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitutive deed, the register of partners, and the prescribed RCS filing form electronically through lbr.lu. Pay the applicable registry fee and provide the specimen signature of the appointed general partner/manager if required by Luxembourg filing practice.
required_dossiers: RCS standard filing form signed by the general partner
Identity and signature specimen of the appointed manager
Consent of the general partner to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of query or refusal, correct the identified omissions within any RCS-determined deadline and resubmit through the same electronic portal; a legal representative may attend the RCS desk if physical signature verification is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the SCSp registration extract in the electronic gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), accessible through lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS issues the registration confirmation, request the mandatory publication of the company deed or an approved extract in RESA. Ensure the publication states the general partner, the registered office, the object, and the persons authorized to bind the partnership.
required_dossiers: Approved extract of the constitutive deed
Publication filing form generated by the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is rejected due to formatting or legal-form discrepancies, obtain an administrative correction order from the RCS and resubmit the amended extract for immediate republication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the business establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale des Classes moyennes, with online intake through guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the administrative form for issuance of the establishment permit for the SCSp or the appointed manager, as required for commercial activity in Luxembourg. Attach the RCS registration extract, managerial competence evidence, and the clean criminal record certificate of the natural person manager.
required_dossiers: Applicant manager's identity card or passport
Professional qualification or managerial experience evidence
Details of the registered office and bank account opening confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, respond within the formal notice period to the Ministry of the Economy; if refused on qualification grounds, lodge a remedy with the administrative tribunal or re-apply with a substitute manager possessing the required establishment credentials.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg social security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), 1105 Luxembourg; online registration via Guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp and any salaried employees with the CCSS after the RCS registration. Declare the general partner and staff in the appropriate social security scheme and request accident insurance and health coverage registration.
required_dossiers: National identification numbers of all partners/employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS unit identifies a mismatch in registration data, transmit a written correction notice through Guichet.lu; retroactive effect may be granted once the corrected declaration is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize VAT and statistical registration with the tax administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg; online through myguichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the VAT registration form (Formulaire 1024) for the SCSp, using the RCS number as the national identifier, and confirm the principal business activity under ISIC 7310. The SCSp may be treated as VAT-exempt or taxable depending on supplies; obtain the official VAT number for invoicing retainer fees and wires.
required_dossiers: Estimated turnover for the first year
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requests further factual information regarding the place of supply or economic activity, provide a supplemental statement of projected clients and services within fifteen days; the VAT certificate is corrected ex tunc once the file is complete.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction Générale des Classes moyennes (General Directorate for Middle Classes) for the business establishment permit; no sector-specific industrial board applies to ISIC 7310.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the trades.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity, Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / registration-only for a non-industrial office-based public relations firm; no full EIA report is required under the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No production discharge thresholds apply; comply with municipal wastewater regulations, EU Directive 2010/75/EU for any combustion plant ancillary to office heating, and the Luxembourg waste management rules for residual office waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office premises under the Regulations of the Grand Ducal police and the Corps Grand-Ducal Incendie et Secours; structural clearance by a certified design engineer for open-to-the-public premises; occupational health and safety inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for workspaces, first-aid, and electrical safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified digital portal MyGuichet.lu and Guichet.lu espace sécurisé (e-Tax).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: File articles of association with Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) via an approved e-filing intermediary; obtain RCS registration and a 14-digit national identification number (NIN). Then register with AEDT for VAT (LU + 8-digit number) before engaging in taxable transactions or within 15 days of first supply; non-resident partners without Luxembourg establishment must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax; partners are taxed in their own capacity on allocated income; the SCSp maintains an independent personality for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; transparency is mandatory. Limited election under Article 176ter LITL allows certain partnerships without legal personality to opt into corporate tax treatment (not conclusively applicable to SCSp due to its legal personality). ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch rules apply under Article 168quater LITL; no discretionary hybrid confirmation election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises under Article 57 VAT exemption (registration optional below threshold, election available); no threshold for non-established foreign suppliers, compulsory registration from the first Luxembourg-taxable transaction; EUR 10,000 turnover threshold for intra-Community distance sales under OSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime in force. B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 January 2020 via PEPPOL/EN 16931 (Law of 22 December 2017 transposing Directive 2014/55/EU). B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary; accepted formats include Factur-X/ZUGFeRD, EDI and hybrid PDF/XML. Invoices must be retained for 10 years; cross-border transaction reporting applies under DAC7/CESOP frameworks.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 52 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for exports of goods to non-EU destinations. B2B services supplied to overseas clients fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the recipient-jurisdiction place-of-supply rule (Article 17 LVD) when the client holds a foreign VAT identification number, resulting in a 0% invoice with mandatory reverse-charge reference and VIES validation. Services directly linked to exported goods are also zero-rated where the recipient is outside the EU. Input VAT refund for EU-related costs is obtained via ordinary VAT returns or AEDT refund procedure per Directive 2008/9/EC.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ELU-AES single administrative document)
Bill of Lading (ocean) / CMR or Air Waybill evidencing departure from EU territory
Proof of customer's foreign VAT status (VIES registration number where applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment proof
Written contract evidencing cross-border supply of PR/communication services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT tax audit division prosecutes fraudulent zero-rating as tax fraud under the General Tax Law: fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years; retrospective reassessment of VAT at 17% plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month (9.6% p.a.) from the original due date; late filing penalties of 10% per month (capped at EUR 1,250) may be stacked. Given SCSp pass-through status, the general partner is jointly and severally liable for VAT clawbacks and partner-level reassessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Central Bank of Luxembourg, operating within the Eurosystem under the policy authority of the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control regime; cross-border capital movements are wholly liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Directive 88/361/EEC. Profit remittance is frictionless: the SCSp is fiscally transparent, so no Luxembourg withholding tax is imposed at entity level on distributions to partners. Residual hurdles are limited to documentary compliance (partner register updates, substance file, and DAC-6/ATAD anti-abuse review where non-resident partners have no economic nexus).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the Eurozone impose no statutory timeline for surrender of export receipts and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to export or service-export proceeds. Inward payments for PR retainers may be held in EUR or any freely chosen currency. Only standard AML/CFT transaction-monitoring obligations apply under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, requiring accurate economic-purpose documentation for each inward credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR current account) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (with dedicated FX and trade-finance sub-limits)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal constraints. A Luxembourg-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution (under the amended Law of 10 August 2018 on payment services, implementing PSD2) may legally hold an operational account for the SCSp without a full banking licence. However, an EMI cannot extend credit, issue Commercial Letters of Credit, or provide collateralised FX hedging lines; the SCSp treasury would therefore require a tier-1 bank counterparty for overdraft, ISDA CSA margining, and LC issuance. Cross-border EMIs passporting into Luxembourg (e.g., Revolut, Wise) may onboard the SCSp remotely, but CSSF AML Circular 12/552 and Regulation 12-02 require the EMI to independently verify the SCSp's ultimate beneficial owners against the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); any mismatch or delay in RBE filing results in frozen onboarding or account restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate for physical board appearance in Luxembourg. CSSF Regulation 12-02 and Circular 12/552 permit risk-based remote onboarding using eIDAS-qualified electronic identification, video identification, and independent source-of-funds verification. In practice, for an SCSp with non-resident corporate partners, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one in-person interview of the general partner's authorised signatories — or a senior manager visit to Luxembourg — unless a local regulated professional (lawyer, notaire, or réviseur d'entreprises agréé) certifies the identity documents and the economic-purpose narrative under a delegated KYC mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp tax-transparency obscuring the chain of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete partnership agreement (contrat de société), deeds of admission for each limited partner, up-to-date extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), passport copies and proof of residence for any partner that is a natural person, and a legal opinion confirming the control chain for corporate partners under the 5% ownership threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners and source-of-funds opacity in the PR retainer flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank references from the partner's home jurisdiction, audited financial statements or tax returns of the partners, a 12-month source-of-wealth statement with supporting disposal/earnings evidence, and a written economic-purpose memorandum signed by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border retainer receipts flagged for mismatch with invoice narrative or low-risk classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed retainer agreements, ISIC 7310 service descriptions, itemised invoices reflecting the EU VAT place-of-supply rules, and SWIFT purpose-code evidence matching the exact invoice reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) identified among partners or PR clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP screening outcome reports, a risk-mitigation declaration, senior management approval minutes, and an enhanced-monitoring undertaking submitted to the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp perceived as a shell-type special LP lacking operational substance in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file comprising: Luxembourg office lease, appointment of a local general partner or management company, payroll records of locally resident staff, board minutes held in Luxembourg, evidence of the bank account in a Luxembourg bank, and annual filings with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident partners arrive via SWIFT MT103 to the dedicated Capital Escrow Account; EUR contributions from EU-based partners may be made through SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001/pain.002). Purpose codes: use ISO 20022 purpose 'CAPI' or EU B2/IC code 7000 with the narrative 'Funds received as capital contributions to a Luxembourg special limited partnership (SCSp)'; for intercompany pre-funding of overseas PR retainers, use purpose 'ICCP' or 'MFGC'. Verification package: executed subscription/contribution deed, capital-call notice signed by the general partner, RBE extract, and confirmation that the beneficiary name on the SWIFT field matches the SCSp's registered name to avoid CSSF Suspicious Transaction Report triggers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for PR operating expenses (media bookings, research subcontracts, crisis-response retainers) use SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001/pain.002) for EU counterparties. For non-EU media vendors and overseas subsidiaries, use SWIFT MT103 (customer payment) with MT202 COV for correspondent bank funding; where documentary conditions apply, a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) is issued to the vendor's confirming bank. For large retainer waterfalls, the treasury relies on SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) for end-to-end tracking, with bank charges allocated as SHA or OUR per the governing contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (OTC, EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex (CSA) collateral
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency PR media invoices and crisis-response costs in emerging markets
Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD) under the ISDA/EMIR framework, either cleared through a central counterparty or subject to bilateral risk-mitigation techniques
FX Swaps (rollover transactions) under EMIR trade-reporting and margining requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial accounts (comptes annuels) for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Partners must approve the accounts within 6 months of the financial year end (by 30 June if FYE 31 December); the approved accounts must be filed with the RCS within 1 month of approval (by 31 July if FYE 31 December).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines of €500–€5,000; after formal notice and continued failure, the RCS may initiate judicial strike-off of the SCSp; the general partner may be held criminally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owner (UBO) registration in the RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the anniversary of the entity's RBE registration; any UBO change must additionally be reported within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to €25,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for deliberate non-compliance; administrative reminder followed by enforcement if confirmation omitted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is required if the SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds in consecutive financial years: total balance sheet €4.4 million, net turnover €8.8 million, and average headcount 50; otherwise exempt from statutory audit but must prepare annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 2009, with optional IFRS for consolidated or unconsolidated accounts where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Within one month after the anniversary of registration in the RBE, the SCSp's registered agent must log in to the Luxembourg Business Registers platform and confirm all UBO details. Share transfers or changes in partner interest must be filed with the RBE within 14 days. The confirmation certifies that the registered data (names, nationalities, ownership percentages) remains current.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate maximum combined corporate income tax rate in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, producing 1.19%, + 6.75% municipal business tax). The Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not independently subject to this headline rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays are available. The dominant preferential feature is entity-level zero taxation of the SCSp due to tax transparency. Partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption, the 80% exemption on qualifying IP income where applicable, and the absence of Luxembourg net wealth tax at the SCSp level.
